questions.solution:
For no sliding &

$f \ge ρav^{2}$
$\mumg \ge ρav^{2}$

options: $K$ is negative, then liquid $A$ and liquid $B$ have convex meniscus.
$K$ is negative, then liquid $A$ and liquid $B$ have concave meniscus.
K is negative, then liquid A has concave meniscus and liquid $B$ has convex meniscus

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{k}=\frac{\cos \theta_{\mathrm{A}}}{\cos \theta_{\mathrm{B}}}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as

Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : A spherical body of radius $( 5 \pm 0 . 1 ) mm$ having a particular density is falling through a liquid of constant density. The percentage error in the calculation of its terminal velocity is $4 %$.

Reason R : The terminal velocity of the spherical body falling through the liquid is inversely proportional to its radius. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$i=96.5 \mathrm{~A}, t=100 \mathrm{~s}w=108Q=i tQ=96.5 \times 100=9650 \mathrm{C}\because 96500$ coulomb deposited wt. of $\mathrm{Ag}=108 \mathrm{~g}\therefore 9650$ coulomb deposited wt. of Ag
$=\frac{108 \times 9650}{96500}$
So, statement $\mathbf{A}$ is true but $\mathbf{R}$ is false. $\mathbf{R}$ is false because mass of substance deposited is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity.

questions.q: A wooden block floating in a bucket of water has $\dfrac{4}{5}$ of its volume submerged. When certain amount of an oil is poured into the bucket, it is found that the block is just under the oil surface with half of its volume under water and half in oil. The density of oil relative to that of water is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Case-1, $\sigmaVg = {ρ}_{w}\dfrac{4}{5}Vg$ …….(I)
Case-2, $\sigmaVg = {ρ}_{w}\dfrac{V}{2}g + {ρ}_{o}\dfrac{V}{2}g$ …….(II)
From eq (I) & (II),
$\dfrac{4}{5}{ρ}_{w} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{w}}{2} + \dfrac{{ρ}_{o}}{2}$
\left(\dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right){ρ}_{w} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{o}}{2}$
\left(\dfrac{8 - 5}{10}\right){ρ}_{w} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{o}}{2}$
$\dfrac{{ρ}_{o}}{{ρ}_{w}} = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6$

questions.q: Two cylindrical vessels of equal cross sectional area of $2 \mathrm{~m}^2$ contain water up to height 10 m and 6 m , respectively. If the vessels are connected at their bottom then the work done by the force of gravity is : (Density of water is $10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ and $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{U}_1=(\rho \mathrm{A} \times 10) \mathrm{g} \times 5+(\rho \mathrm{A} 6) \mathrm{g} \times 3 \\ & \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=\rho \mathrm{Ag}(50+18) \\ & \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=68 \rho \mathrm{Ag}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & U_f=(\rho A \times 16) g \times 4 \\ & =(\rho A g) \times 64\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \omega=\Delta U=4 \times \rho A g \\ & =4 \times 1000 \times 2 \times 10=8 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An ideal fluid flows (laminar flow) through a pipe of non-uniform diameter. The maximum and minimum diameters of the pipes are $6.4$ cm and $4.8$ cm , respectively. The ratio of the minimum and the maximum velocities of fluid in this pipe is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using equation of continuity
${A}_{1}{V}_{1} = {A}_{2}{V}_{2}$
$\dfrac{V1}{V2} = \dfrac{A2}{A1} = \left(\dfrac{4.8}{6.4}\right)2 = \dfrac{9}{16}$

questions.q:
A water drop of radius $1$ cm is broken into $729$ equal droplets. If surface tension of water is $75dyne{cm}^{- 1}$, then the gain in surface energy upto first decimal place will be

[Given $\pi = 3 . 14$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The volume of the bigger drop will be,& $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}$. If the radius of smaller drops is~$r$, using the conservation of volume,

$n\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} ⇒ 729 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} ⇒ r = \dfrac{R}{9}$

The initial surface energy will be,

${E}_{i} = \left(4\piR^{2}\right)T$~

And final surface energy will be,

${E}_{f} = n\left(4\pir^{2}\right)T = 729 \times 4\pi\left(\dfrac{R}{9}\right)2T= 36\piR^{2}T$

Therefore, the change in the surface energy will be,

$⇒ \Delta E = {E}_{f} - {E}_{i} = 32\piR^{2}T = 32 \times 3 . 14 \times \left(1 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)2 \times 75 \times {10}^{- 3} ⇒ \Delta E = 7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}J$

questions.q:
A cubical block of side $0.5m$ floats on water with $30%$ of its volume under water. What is the maximum weight that can be put on the block without fully submerging it under water?

[Take, density of water $= {10}^{3}kg / m^{3}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In first case, when $30%$ of the cube inside water,
${ρ}_{w}{V}_{in}g = {ρ}_{c}Vg$
$\dfrac{{V}_{in}}{V} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{c}}{{ρ}_{w}} = 0.3$
Additional weight we can put $w$ is,
$V{ρ}_{w}g = {ρ}_{c}Vg + w$
$w = V\left({ρ}_{w} - {ρ}_{c}\right)g$
$= {\left(0.5\right)}^{3} \times 0.7 \times {10}^{3} \times g$
$= 87.5gN$
Addition of mass that we can put $= 87.5kg$

questions.q: The velocity of a small ball of mass $m$~and density ${d}_{1}$, when dropped in a container filled with glycerine, becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is ${d}_{2}$, then the viscous force acting on the ball, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At the time of terminal velocity ball is in equilibrium i.e.& ${F}_{g} = {F}_{b} + {F}_{v}$

$⇒ {F}_{v} = {F}_{g} - {F}_{b}$

$⇒ {F}_{v} = mg - {d}_{2}\dfrac{m}{d1}g$

$⇒ mg \left($1 - \dfrac{d2}{d1}\right)$

$

questions.q:
Pressure inside a soap bubble is greater than the pressure outside by an amount :
(given : $\mathrm{R}=$ Radius of bubble $\mathrm{S}=$ Surface tension of bubble)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
There are two liquid-air surfaces in bubble so
$\Delta \mathrm{P}=2\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{~S}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)=\frac{4 \mathrm{~S}}{\mathrm{R}}$

questions.q: Water flows m a horizontal tube (see figure). The pressure of water changes by $700Nm^{- 2}$ between $A$ and $B$ where the area of cross section are $40cm^{2}$ and $20cm^{2},$ respectively. Find the rate of flow of water through the tube. (density of water $= 1000kgm^{- 3}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using equation of continuity
$40{V}_{A} = 20{V}_{B}$
$⇒ 2{V}_{A} = {V}_{B}$
Using Bernoulli’s equation
${P}_{A} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_A^{2} = {P}_{B} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_B^{2}$
$⇒ {P}_{A} - {P}_{B} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left({V}_B^{2} - {V}_A^{2}\right)
$⇒ $\Delta$P = $\dfrac{1}{2}$1000 \left({V}_B^{2} - \dfrac{{V}_B^{2}}{4}\right)$
$⇒ \Delta P = 500 \times \dfrac{3{V}_B^{2}}{4}$
$⇒ {V}_{B} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\left(\Delta P\right) \times 4}{1500}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\left(700\right) \times 4}{1500}}\dfrac{m}{s}$
Volume flow rate $= 20 \times100 \times {V}_{B} =2732cm^{3} / s$

questions.q: A hydraulic automobile lift is designed to lift vehicles of mass $5000$ kg. The area of cross section of the cylinder carrying load is $250{cm}^{2}$. The maximum pressure the smaller piston would have to bear is [Assume $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is

$m = 5000kgg = 10ms^{- 2}A = 250 \times {10}^{- 4}m^{2}$

Using the formula of pressure,

$P = \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{mg}{A}$
$= \dfrac{5000 \times 10}{250 \times {10}^{- 4}}$

$= 2 \times {10}^{6}Nm^{- 2} = 2 \times {10}^{6}Pa$

questions.q: A small spherical ball of radius $r$, falling through a viscous medium of negligible density has terminal velocity $v$. Another ball of the same mass but of radius $2r$, falling through the same viscous medium will have terminal velocity:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Ignoring buoyancy force, we can write terminal velocity as

$mg = 6\piηrv$

$⇒ v ∝ \dfrac{1}{r}$ (as mass is constant)

Now, $\dfrac{v}{v '} = \dfrac{r '}{r}$

$\text{As}r ' = 2r$

So $v ' = \dfrac{v}{2}$

questions.q: A small ball of mass $M$ and density~$ρ$~is dropped in a viscous liquid of density~${ρ}_{0}$. After some time, the ball falls with a constant velocity. What is the viscous force on the ball?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The buoyant force is given by&

$B = V{ρ}_{0}g$

where~$V$~is the volume of the ball. The weight of the ball

$W = Mg = Vρg$, is acting in the opposite direction of the buoyant force . Hence, at terminal velocity

$Mg - B = {F}_{v}$

$⇒ B + {F}_{v} = Mg$

$⇒ {F}_{v} = Vρg - V{ρ}_{0}g ⇒ {F}_{v} = ρVg ( 1 - \dfrac{ρ0}{ρ} ) ⇒ {F}_{v} = Mg ( 1 - \dfrac{ρ0}{ρ} )$

questions.q:
A capillary tube of radius 0.1 mm is partly dipped in water (surface tension $70 \mathrm{dyn} / \mathrm{cm}$ and glass water contact angle $\simeq 0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$) with $30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ inclined with vertical. The length of water risen in the capillary is ________ cm.
\left(\right.$ Take \left.\mathrm{g}=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{h}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T} \cos \theta}{\rho \mathrm{gr}}=\frac{2 \times 70 \times 1}{1 \times 980 \times 10^{-2}} \\ & \mathrm{~h}=\frac{100}{7} \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \sin 60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\ell} \\ & \ell=\frac{\mathrm{h} \times 2}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & \ell=\frac{100}{7} \times \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & =\frac{200}{7 \times \sqrt{3}} \\ & =16.49 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Water from a tap emerges vertically downwards with an initial speed of $1.0ms^{- 1}$ . The cross $-$ sectional area of the tap is ${10}^{- 4}m^{2}$ . Assume that the pressure is constant throughout the stream of water and that the flow is streamlined. The cross $-$ sectional area of the stream, $0.15m$ below the tap would be:
(Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Velocity of water after falling through distance $0.15m$ is
$v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$
$= 1 + 2 \times 10 \times 0.15$
$v^{2} = 4$
$v = 2m / s$
From equation of continuity
${A}_{1}{v}_{1} = {A}_{2}{v}_{2}$
${A}_{2} = \dfrac{{10}^{- 4} \times 1}{2} = 5 \times {10}^{- 5}m^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : Viscosity of gases is greater than that of liquids.

Statement (II) : Surface tension of a liquid decreases due to the presence of insoluble impurities.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Viscosity is a measure of a fluid's resistance to flow, and gases typically have lower molecular interactions and are less dense than liquids, resulting in lower viscosity.

The presence of insoluble impurities in a liquid can decrease its surface tension. Surface tension is related to the cohesive forces between molecules at the surface of a liquid. Insoluble impurities can disrupt these cohesive forces, leading to a decrease in surface tension.

Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: Figure below shows a liquid being pushed out of the tube by a piston having area of cross section $2 . 0{cm}^{2}$. The area of cross section at the outlet is $10{mm}^{2}$. If the piston is pushed at a speed of $4cms^{- 1}$, the speed of outgoing fluid is _____~$cms^{- 1}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is&

${A}_{1} = 2 \times {10}^{- 4}m^{2}{A}_{2} = 10 \times {10}^{- 6}m^{2}{v}_{1} = 4cms^{- 1}$

Using equation of continuity which is a conservation of mass principle,

${A}_{1}{v}_{1} = {A}_{2}{v}_{2}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = \dfrac{{A}_{1}{v}_{1}}{A2} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 4}{10 \times {10}^{- 6}}$

$= 80cms^{- 1}$

questions.q: When a long glass capillary tube of radius& $0 . 015cm$ is dipped in a liquid, the liquid rises to a height of~$15$ cm within it. If the contact angle between the liquid and glass to close to $0 °$, the surface tension of the liquid, in milliNewton~$m^{- 1},$ is~  \left[{ρ}_{(liqued) } = 900kgm^{- 3}, g = 10ms^{- 2}\right]$ (Given answer in closed integer)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using the concept of rise due to surface tension,

& $\dfrac{2T}{r} = hρg$

$T = \dfrac{rhρg}{2} = \dfrac{15 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 15 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 900 \times 10}{2} = 101milliNewtonm^{- 1}$

questions.q: A tube of length 1 m is filled completely with an ideal liquid of mass 2 M , and closed at both ends. The tube is rotated uniformly in horizontal plane about one of its ends. If the force exerted by the liquid at the other end is F then angular velocity of the tube is $\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\alpha \mathrm{M}}}$ in SI unit. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: \(\begin{aligned} & F=m \omega^2 $r_{\mathrm{cm}}$\\ & $r_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}$\\ & \$omega=\sqrt{\frac{2 F}{m}}$\\ & m=2 M \\ & \$omega=\sqrt{\frac{F}{M}}$\\ & \alpha=1\end{aligned}\)

questions.q:
The velocity of a small ball of mass $0 . 3g$~and density $8g{cc}^{- 1}$ when dropped in a container filled with glycerine becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is $1 . 3g{cc}^{- 1}$, then the value of viscous force acting on the ball will be $x \times {10}^{- 4}N$, the value of $x$ is _____ .

[use $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& ${F}_{V}$~be the viscous force and~${F}_{B}$~be the buoyant force acting on the ball.

Then, when body moves with constant velocity,

${F}_{V} + {F}_{B} = Mg$~ ~

Or,~${F}_{V} = Mg - {F}_{B}$

${F}_{V} = {ρ}_{B}Vg - {ρ}_{L}Vg$~$= \left({ρ}_{B} -\right)\left({ρ}_{L}\right)Vg$, where,~$V$~is the volume of small ball.

$= \left(8 - 1 . 3\right) × {10}^{3} × \dfrac{0 . 3 × {10}^{- 3}}{8 × {10}^{3}} × 10$

$= \dfrac{6 . 7 × 0 . 3}{8} × {10}^{- 2}$

$= \dfrac{67 × 3}{8} × {10}^{- 4} = 25 . 125 × {10}^{- 4} = 25 × {10}^{- 4}N$

Thus, the value of~$x = 25$.

questions.q: The water is filled up to a height of $12m$ in a tank having vertical sidewalls. A hole is made in one of the walls at a depth~$h$ below the water level. The value of~$h$ for which the emerging stream of water strikes the ground at the maximum range is _____~$m$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$R = \sqrt{2gh} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{( 12 - h ) \times 2}{g}}$

$\sqrt{4h ( 12 - h )} = R$

For maximum $R$

$\dfrac{dR}{dh} = 0$

$⇒ h = 6m$
